---
title: "Evaluate Static Capacitance"
subtitle: "Inspect the finite capacitance matrix and explicit zero-charge reductions"
toc-depth: 2
---

The [Static Capacitance Contract](../contracts/static-capacitance.qmd) defines
the candidate API and its failure boundary. This guide shows how to request the
matrix or a coordinate entry at one physical point, then differentiate the
same declaration.

## Evaluate the compiled matrix

Reuse a sealed Plan, its original View or an existing coordinate-transform-only
View, and one effective parameter point. The static matrix is bound to the
same compiled finite model as that request; it includes the finite-pi
capacitance of any discretized transmission line.

```python
from scnsim import StaticCapacitanceSpec

capacitance_spec = StaticCapacitanceSpec()
matrix_result = run.evaluate(
    view,
    capacitance_spec,
    parameters=point,
)
capacitance = matrix_result.matrix.to("farad")
```

`matrix_result.row_coordinates` and `matrix_result.column_coordinates` give the
ordered compiled node-coordinate IDs for the two matrix axes. The matrix covers
that complete coordinate basis, including internal non-Port coordinates.
`matrix_result.evidence` binds its Plan, effective parameter point, selected
View, dtype, and finite discretization. This is a capacitance matrix, not a
frequency-indexed response.
The returned row and column IDs, including internal finite-pi axes, can be
reused for a static element or `zero_charge` request only with the same Plan,
View, parameter point, and realized mesh. These IDs address static result axes;
they do not create public coordinate refs or enable internal-node RF selection
or `retain()`.

For an existing paired-coordinate View, the runtime resolves its actual
parameter-dependent real transform $T(\theta)$ and evaluates
$C_y=T(\theta)^T C_x(\theta)T(\theta)$. The transformation changes the
coordinate representation; it does not rewire the Plan. No PTC or retained
View is substituted into this request.

## Request a zero-charge reduction

Name every coordinate whose charge is constrained to zero. The remaining
coordinates retain their order from the selected View:

```python
reduced_spec = StaticCapacitanceSpec(
    zero_charge=(eliminated_coordinate,),
)
reduced_result = run.evaluate(view, reduced_spec, parameters=point)
effective_capacitance = reduced_result.matrix.to("farad")
```

With $r$ denoting the retained coordinates and $e$ the explicit eliminated
coordinates, the operation uses

$$
C_{\mathrm{eff}}=C_{rr}-C_{re}\,\operatorname{solve}(C_{ee},C_{er}),
\qquad q_e=0.
$$

Inspect `reduced_result.zero_charge` and its row/column coordinate IDs alongside
the matrix. This is a zero-charge boundary, not a voltage clamp, physical
ground, or guessed node. A singular full matrix may still be exported. If the
selected $C_{ee}$ block cannot be solved, the request reports that native
failure; it does not substitute a pseudoinverse or regularize the block.

## Select one coordinate entry

The `column` keyword is deliberate and names the second matrix axis:

```python
entry_spec = capacitance_spec.element(
    row=row_coordinate,
    column=column_coordinate,
)
entry_result = run.evaluate(view, entry_spec, parameters=point)
entry = entry_result.value.to("farad")
```

The element result preserves `row`, `column`, `zero_charge`, and the same
Plan/point/View/discretization provenance as a matrix result. For an element of
a reduced matrix, construct the element from the spec that carries the desired
`zero_charge` partition.

## Differentiate the same matrix or element

For sensitivities, use the selector on the same View and the same effective
point. For example, a Jacobian differentiates each matrix entry with respect to
the ordered physical parameter list:

```python
from scnsim import Jacobian, SensitivitySpec

sensitivity_spec = SensitivitySpec(
    quantities={"C": capacitance_spec.matrix.on(view)},
    wrt=(capacitance_parameter,),
    derivative=Jacobian(),
    discretization=fixed_mesh,
)
jacobian_result = run.sensitivity(
    sensitivity_spec,
    parameters=point,
)
```

For an element, bind `entry_spec.value.on(view)` as the quantity instead. The
existing JVP and VJP declarations work on either selected quantity. Their
directions and weights follow the ordinary physical-unit rules in the
[Sensitivity guide](sensitivity.qmd); the static-C outputs have units of
farads. A raw matrix Jacobian therefore has units F per SI unit of the input;
when the input is itself measured in F, the cell is dimensionless by unit
cancellation, not by automatic sensitivity normalization. Derivatives pass
through the parameter-dependent $C(\theta)$, resolved $T(\theta)$, and the
actual elimination solve. The transform weights are not replaced by baseline
constants.

Use one fixed realized finite mesh for the sensitivity request. The derivative
does not differentiate an integer line-section choice. The initial
static-capacitance backend is JAX; selecting Julia for this quantity reports an
unsupported capability rather than rerunning the calculation through another
backend.

Memory and Workspace results expose the same static matrix and element value
interfaces. Memory results are detached; Workspace results use fixed selected
readers and may be inspected after `run.close()`. Existing Julia operations
and the current dynamic response, root, and residue-normalized-coupling
contracts are unchanged.
